STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate, square-ish white plate with a rim band and flat centre.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plate, medium-large. Typical 20-30 cm.
b) Reference: broccoli florets are about 4 cm. The plate spans roughly 7-8 florets across the long side, so roughly 28-30 cm. The plate also looks about twice the length of the scrambled egg mound, which suggests about 22-26 cm. I trust the reference-object estimate more, so width is about 25 cm.

Area: square plate, 25 x 25 = 625 cm2. Food covers about 60% of it.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg: mound covering about 22% of the plate, about 137 cm2. Mound thickness about 2 cm average (peak about 3-4 cm). Volume = 137 x 2 = 274 ml. Density 0.8, so about 220 g.
- Strawberries (sliced): about 8% of plate, about 50 cm2, flat-ish layer about 1.2 cm thick. Volume about 60 ml. Density 0.6, so about 36 g.
- Spinach (cooked-looking wilted leaves, some raw): about 15% of plate, about 94 cm2, layer about 1.5 cm. Volume about 140 ml. Density 0.6 (cooked), so about 85 g.
- Broccoli florets: about 8% of plate, about 50 cm2, about 2.5 cm thick. Volume about 125 ml. Density 0.6, so about 75 g.

Hidden food: no clear base layer under the egg; the plate surface appears visible, so no extra items.

STEP 4 - Total is about 220 + 36 + 85 + 75 = 416 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Scrambled egg (with some butter/oil): about 150 kcal/100 g.
- Strawberries: about 32 kcal/100 g.
- Spinach, cooked: about 23 kcal/100 g.
- Broccoli, cooked: about 35 kcal/100 g.

Energy: egg 220 g x 1.5 = 330 kcal; strawberries 36 g x 0.32 = 12 kcal; spinach 85 g x 0.23 = 20 kcal; broccoli 75 g x 0.35 = 26 kcal. Total about 388 kcal.
